summary: The Score distribution panel on the overview: 21 bars, one per possible risk score (0, 5, … 100), each coloured by its risk level, with dashed markers at the 30, 60 and 80 thresholds. Heights use a square-root scale so the rare high scores stay visible next to the pile of low ones. Its data is `score_histogram` from iip/queries.py; it redraws through `responsive` from charts/core.js and uses the shared tooltip.

notes.text: Header comment. Rule weights are multiples of 5, so a score can only be 0, 5, 10 … 100 and the chart gets exactly one bar per possible score; bars are coloured by level, thresholds are marked, and a √ scale keeps the long tail visible.
Imports: escaping and number formatting from dom.js, `animate` and `stagger` from motion.js, the shared tooltip, and `responsive` from charts/core.js.
`scoreHistogram(el, buckets, options)`. Each bucket is `{ score, value, level }` from the API; the default thresholds 30, 60 and 80 are where MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL begin.
Draws through `responsive`, so the chart fits its container and redraws on resize; the overview registers the returned cleanup with `ctx.add`.
Padding (extra room on top for the threshold numbers) and the inner plot width and height.
`band` is the horizontal slot each bucket gets: the plot width shared evenly between the buckets.

The scale's maximum is the **square root** of the largest count (at least 1), and bars compare square roots too. If score 0 has 900 events and score 85 has 4, a linear scale shrinks the 4 to under 0.5% of the height, while √4 / √900 is about 7%, so differences among the rare high scores stay readable (the panel carries a √ scale tag so nobody misreads it).
`base` is the y of the baseline; bars grow upward from it.
`xOf(score)` gives the x of the left edge of a score's slot: score / 5 is the bucket index, times the slot width.
For each bucket the height is √count divided by √max, times the plot height. Empty buckets get no bar, and any non-empty bucket is at least 2 px tall so a single event still shows.

Each bar is a `rect` with class `lvl-LEVEL`, which charts.css fills with `var(--lvl)` (variables work in CSS rules, just not reliably in attributes). It is inset 18% on each side of its slot to leave gaps; `data-i` lets the tooltip find the bucket and `data-h` stores the final height for the animation.

Threshold markers: for each threshold, a vertical line (dashed by charts.css) at the left edge of that score's slot, exactly where the new level begins, rising 8 px above the plot with the number printed beside its top.
Opens the SVG at the measured width with a matching `viewBox`, plus `role="img"` and an `aria-label` for screen readers.
The baseline along the bottom of the plot.
Threshold markers first, then bars, so the bars paint over the dashed lines.
X-axis labels at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100, each centred under its score's bar (`xOf(s) + band / 2`).
Closes the SVG template.
Keeps a reference to the new SVG.

One `pointermove` listener on the whole SVG (event delegation) instead of one per bar: `closest("rect.bar")` finds the bar under the pointer, and if there is none the tooltip is hidden; `return hideTip()` hides and exits in one statement.
Looks up the bucket via the bar's `data-i` (a string, which still works as an array index) and shows its score, event count and level. The closing `});` ends the handler.
Hides the tooltip when the pointer leaves the chart.
First draw only: collects the bars into an array.

Animates every bar from zero height to its stored height. SVG rects grow downward from their `y`, so `y` moves from the baseline up to `base - h` at the same time, making the bars rise from the baseline; the functions `(r) => [...]` give each bar its own start and end values.
900 ms with the decelerating `outExpo` ease, each bar starting 22 ms after the previous one (from 150 ms) via `stagger`, so a wave runs left to right. The closing lines end the call and the `if`.
Closes the `responsive` callback and `scoreHistogram`.
